title: Baby Shawl in Shell Stitch
subtitle: DK weight shell stitch squares worked in the round for a 80cm x 80cm baby shawl
excerpt: A square baby shawl for a 0 to 6 month old, worked from the centre outward in shell stitch. Each shell is 5 trebles in a single chain space. DK weight on a 4mm hook produces a fabric soft enough for a newborn but structured enough to hold its shape.
sourceNotes: Original pattern synthesised for Homemade. Centre-out square construction with shell edging is a well-established baby shawl technique with no single originating source.
heroPrompt: A square baby shawl in white DK yarn with a shell stitch pattern. Laid flat on a cream linen surface with a small teddy bear placed in one corner. Soft daylight, delicate styling.

glossaryTerms.definition: A group of treble crochets worked into the same stitch or space to form a fan shape. In this pattern each shell is 5 trebles worked into a single chain space.
The gap created by a chain between stitches. You work into the space itself, not into the individual chain stitches.
An adjustable loop start: yarn is wrapped into a ring, the first round of stitches is worked into it, then the tail is pulled to close the centre. Produces a neat, tight centre with no hole.

content.text: This baby shawl is an 80cm square worked from the centre outward in rounds using shell stitch. It is sized for a 0 to 6 month old infant. Each shell is 5 trebles worked into a single chain space. You begin with a magic ring, work an initial set of shells in the first round, then increase by adding corner shells on every subsequent round. The technique is the same throughout: shell into each chain space from the previous round, plus an extra shell at each corner. DK weight on a 4mm hook produces fabric that is soft against newborn skin and firm enough to wrap securely. The square shape is practical: it can be folded on the diagonal as a triangle or laid flat as a swaddle.

Yarn: approximately 350g of DK weight yarn. For a baby item, use a machine-washable yarn with a soft finish. Pure cotton, bamboo-cotton, or superwash merino work well. Hook: 4mm. You will also need a tapestry needle, scissors, a tape measure, and optional stitch markers and blocking mat.

One shell (5 tr) measures approximately 3.5cm wide on a 4mm hook over shell stitch. Tension is not critical for a baby shawl, but if your tension is tighter than stated the finished piece will be smaller than 80cm square. Work a small swatch in shell stitch to check.
Shell: 5 tr in same ch sp

The shawl is worked in joined rounds from the centre. A corner is formed by working ch 2 between two shells into the same chain space. Each corner chain space appears at the same position every round. Use stitch markers on the corner chain spaces if helpful.
Ch 4 (counts as tr + ch 1), [shell in ring, ch 2] 4 times, sl st to 3rd ch of starting ch-4 to join. Pull magic ring tail to close centre. (4 shells, 4 corner ch-2 sps)

Sl st into first ch-2 corner sp, ch 4 (counts as tr + ch 1), shell in same corner sp, ch 1, [shell in corner ch-2 sp, ch 2, shell in same corner ch-2 sp, ch 1] 3 times, sl st to 3rd ch of starting ch-4. (8 shells)

Sl st into corner sp, ch 4, shell in same corner sp, ch 1, shell in side ch-1 sp, ch 1, [shell in corner sp, ch 2, shell in same corner sp, ch 1, shell in side ch-1 sp, ch 1] 3 times, sl st to join. (12 shells)

Each round adds 4 shells (one extra side shell per side). Work [shell in corner sp, ch 2, shell in same corner sp, ch 1] at every corner, and [shell in each ch-1 sp along each side, ch 1] between corners. Continue until the square measures approximately 80cm on each side. End with a sl st join. Fasten off.
Work one round of dc evenly around all four sides, placing 3 dc into each corner ch-2 sp. Sl st to join, fasten off.

Weave in all ends on the wrong side using the tapestry needle. Block by soaking in cool water, pressing out excess moisture in a towel, then pinning the four corners and sides square on a foam mat. Allow to dry completely. Make sure there are no loose tails that could unravel and be dangerous for a baby.
Machine wash on a gentle cool cycle if you have used a superwash or cotton yarn. Check the yarn label for the specific fibre. Dry flat to maintain the square shape. Do not tumble dry.

Once the centre-out square technique feels comfortable, try a baby blanket using the same method with a larger hook and bulkier yarn. For a more formal baby shawl, the baby christening shawl uses lace weight on a 2.5mm hook with a dc mesh body and shell border. For an adult garment using the same shell-over-chain-space principle, see the classic prayer shawl.
